root_cause_label: Hardcoded Wrong ELF Base Address with No Programmatic Parsing
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent hardcoded a spurious 0x400000 base address offset in step 6 without deriving VMA-to-file-offset mappings from the ELF headers, then spent the rest of the trajectory thrashing through parsing variants and a final brute-force whole-file read, none of which produced correct output.
t_err_evidence: In step 6, the agent writes extract.js using hardcoded section addresses 0x402000 (.rodata) and 0x404000 (.data) — derived by adding an assumed 0x400000 base to the section VMAs — even though the ELF section headers from step 2 show the actual VMAs are 0x2000 and 0x4000 with no such base. This false-premise base addition is the decisive wrong action.
t_commit_evidence: Once the agent committed to the 0x400000-base address scheme in step 6, all subsequent iterations (steps 7-26) were variations on the same wrong address model; no step correctly re-derived the address mapping from ELF headers, locking in the failure from step 6 onward.
t_surface_evidence: Step 7 produces output with addresses 4202496 (0x402000) and 4210688 (0x404000) and integer values that do not match the expected output, providing the first observable failure signal.
trigger_explanation: The agent assumed a standard PIE 0x400000 load base and added it to the relative VMAs seen in readelf output, yielding 0x402000 and 0x404000. In reality the ELF's VMAs (0x2000, 0x4000) already are the correct virtual addresses for non-PIE sections; the correct approach was to read the section VMA and file offset directly from the ELF headers and map file bytes to those VMAs without adding any extra base.
fabrication_evidence: Instead of programmatically parsing ELF section headers at runtime, the agent hardcoded section base addresses (0x402000, 0x404000) as magic constants inferred by manual inspection, bypassing the correct ELF parsing the task requires. Later, in step 24-26, it further shortcuts by reading the entire binary as a flat memory block at 0x400000, which is an even more drastic misrepresentation of ELF memory layout.
